seo.shortDescription: Searchable duty table for all 50 HTS Chapter 49 lines: books, newspapers, magazines, children's books, maps, sheet music, decals, greeting cards, calendars, catalogs and posters. Every base rate is Free; see the 2026 Section 301 duty by country and the informational-materials exemption.

overview.intro:
Chapter 49 covers the products of the printing industry: **books and brochures** (4901), **newspapers and magazines** (4902), **children's picture books** (4903), sheet music, maps and globes, hand-drawn plans, unused stamps and banknotes, **decals** (4908), **postcards and greeting cards** (4909), **calendars** (4910) and other printed matter — catalogs, posters, pictures and photographs (4911). Every one of its **50 tariff lines is Free** at the general rate.

The extra duty by country decides the cost. Since **July 24, 2026** goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%**, but **informational materials** such as books, newspapers, maps and posters can be entered under 9903.05.92 and pay none of it. China keeps its 2019 Section 301 List 4A duty of **7.5%** on most printed matter, which has no such exemption. Canada pays a **50% Section 338 duty** on non-lithographic pictures and decals even with a USMCA claim. China supplied 42% of the $5.16B imported in 2025.

productGroups.label: Printed books, brochures, leaflets & similar printed matter
productGroups.blurb: Books of every kind — textbooks, dictionaries, bibles and religious books, technical books, art books, hardbacks and paperbacks — plus brochures, leaflets and single printed sheets. All Free. 44% of 2025 imports ($2.28B). Brochures devoted to advertising, such as trade catalogs, are heading 4911 (chapter note 5).

productGroups.label: Newspapers, journals & periodicals
productGroups.blurb: Newspapers, journals and periodicals, unbound: dailies appearing at least four times a week (4902.10), other newspapers, business and professional journals and magazines (4902.90.20). All Free; newspaper supplements printed by gravure carry a 25% column 2 rate. Bound volumes are heading 4901.

productGroups.label: Children's picture, drawing & coloring books
productGroups.blurb: Children's picture, drawing and coloring books — books in which the pictures are the main interest and the text is subsidiary (chapter note 6). Free. China shipped $455M of the $506M imported in 2025, and this line is on no active China Section 301 list.

productGroups.label: Printed or manuscript music
productGroups.blurb: Printed or manuscript music, bound or not: sheet music (4904.00.00.20) and music books. Free.

productGroups.label: Maps, charts, atlases & globes
productGroups.blurb: Printed maps, hydrographic charts and atlases in book form (4905.20), globes (4905.90.20) and wall maps and other charts (4905.90.60). Free. Maps or globes in relief are heading 9023.

productGroups.label: Hand-drawn plans & drawings, manuscripts and their copies
productGroups.blurb: Original hand-drawn architectural, engineering and industrial plans and drawings, hand-written texts, and photographic or carbon copies of them. Free.

productGroups.label: Unused stamps, banknotes, cheque forms, stock certificates
productGroups.blurb: Unused postage and revenue stamps of current issue in the country where they are valid, stamp-impressed paper, banknotes, cheque forms, and stock, share or bond certificates. Free; currency and securities imported for monetary purposes need no formal entry (additional U.S. note 2). Used or collectors' stamps are heading 9704.

productGroups.label: Transfers (decals)
productGroups.blurb: Transfers (decalcomanias): vitrifiable decals for ceramics and glass (4908.10) and other decals (4908.90), such as water-slide and dry-transfer designs. Free; Canadian 4908.90 decals pay the 50% Section 338 duty.

productGroups.label: Postcards & greeting cards
productGroups.blurb: Printed or illustrated postcards (4909.00.20) and printed cards bearing greetings, messages or announcements, with or without envelopes (4909.00.40) — birthday, Christmas and wedding cards. Free. Vietnam's largest Chapter 49 line.

productGroups.label: Printed calendars
productGroups.blurb: Calendars of any kind, including calendar blocks: lithographed on paper up to 0.51 mm (4910.00.20) or thicker (4910.00.40), and other calendars (4910.00.60). Free.

productGroups.label: Other printed matter: catalogs, posters, pictures, photos, forms
productGroups.blurb: Everything else printed: trade catalogs, price lists and tourist literature (4911.10), pictures, designs, prints, posters and photographs (4911.91), and other printed matter such as forms, tickets and carnets (4911.99). Free. 34% of 2025 imports ($1.74B); original engravings and prints are heading 9702.

workedExamples.title: A pallet of hardback novels from the United Kingdom
workedExamples.body: Hardbound books are Free at the general rate. The UK's 2026 Section 301 rate is 10% (9903.05.81), but books are informational materials: entered under 9903.05.92, a $20,000 shipment pays **$0** duty. Without that claim it would pay $2,000.

workedExamples.title: Printed books from China
workedExamples.body: Most of 4901.99.00 is on China Section 301 List 4A (9903.88.15, U.S. note 20(s)(ii)), which charges **7.5%** and has no informational-materials exemption: **$750** on a $10,000 shipment. The 2026 Section 301 duty of 12.5% (9903.05.31) is lifted by claiming 9903.05.92; without the claim the total is $2,000. Bibles and other religious books (4901.99.00.40) are excluded from List 4A, so with the claim they pay $0.

workedExamples.title: Children's coloring books from China
workedExamples.body: 4903.00.00 was put on List 4B, which has been suspended since December 2019, so no China Section 301 list duty applies. Entered as informational materials under 9903.05.92, a $10,000 shipment pays **$0**; without the claim it pays the 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty, $1,250. China supplied 90% of U.S. imports of these books in 2025.

workedExamples.title: Decals from Canada, with a USMCA claim
workedExamples.body: Non-vitrifiable decals printed in Canada qualify for USMCA (a change from any other chapter), which removes Canada's 10% Section 301 duty (9903.05.93). But 4908.90.00 is on the Section 338 list (U.S. note 51(b)(3), 9903.03.14), and that 50% applies even under USMCA and has no informational-materials exemption: **$5,000** on $10,000.

notes.chapterNotes:
**Note 1.** This chapter does not cover: (a) photographic negatives or positives on transparent bases (chapter 37); (b) maps, plans or globes, in relief, whether or not printed (heading 9023); (c) playing cards or other goods of chapter 95; or (d) original engravings, prints or lithographs (heading 9702), postage or revenue stamps, stamp-postmarks, first-day covers, postal stationery or the like of heading 9704, antiques of an age exceeding one hundred years or other articles of chapter 97.

**Note 2.** For the purposes of chapter 49 the term "printed" also means reproduced by means of a duplicating machine, produced under the control of an automatic data processing machine, embossed, photographed, photocopied, thermocopied or typewritten.

**Note 3.** Newspapers, journals and periodicals which are bound otherwise than in paper, and sets of newspapers, journals or periodicals comprising more than one issue under a single cover are to be classified in heading 4901, whether or not containing advertising material.

**Note 4.** Heading 4901 also covers: (a) a collection of printed reproductions of, for example, works of art or drawings, with a relative text, put up with numbered pages in a form suitable for binding into one or more volumes; (b) a pictorial supplement accompanying and subsidiary to a bound volume; and (c) printed parts of books or booklets, in the form of assembled or separate sheets or signatures, constituting the whole or a part of a complete work and designed for binding. However, printed pictures or illustrations not bearing a text, whether in the form of signatures or separate sheets, fall in heading 4911.

**Note 5.** Subject to note 3 of this chapter, heading 4901 does not cover publications which are essentially devoted to advertising (for example, brochures, pamphlets, leaflets, trade catalogs, yearbooks published by trade associations and tourist promotional literature). Such publications are to be classified in heading 4911.

**Note 6.** For the purposes of heading 4903, the expression "children's picture books" means books for children in which the pictures form the principal interest and the text is subsidiary.
notes.additionalUsNotes:
**1.** For the purposes of determining the classification of printed matter produced in whole or in part by a lithographic process, the thickness of such printed matter is that of the thinnest paper contained therein, except that the thickness of a permanently mounted lithograph is the combined thickness of the lithograph and its mounting.

**2.** Currency in current circulation in any country imported for monetary purposes and securities and similar evidences of value provided for in heading 4907 shall be admitted without formal customs consumption entry or the payment of duty. This does not affect any requirement under other provisions of law to the effect that transfers of monetary instruments into or through the United States, in an amount exceeding $10,000 on any one occasion, shall be reported as prescribed therein.

seo.shortDescription: What changed for books, newspapers and other printed matter (HTS Chapter 49) since January 2025: unchanged Free base rates, the informational-materials exemption from the IEEPA, Section 122 and 2026 Section 301 tariffs, China's 7.5% List 4A duty, Canada's 50% Section 338 duty and the end of de minimis.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). All 50 Chapter 49 lines are **Free** in both.

What changed came on top of the base rate — and for printed matter, mostly did not reach it. The law behind the 2025 IEEPA tariffs bars regulating **informational materials** (50 U.S.C. 1702(b)(3)), so books, newspapers and similar goods were excepted until those duties **ended on February 24, 2026**. The Section 122 surcharge that followed (to July 23, 2026) and the **2026 Section 301 tariffs** on 60 economies (from July 24, 2026) and on Brazil (from July 22, 2026) repeat that exception: importers claim **9903.05.92** (and 9903.05.09 for Brazil). Duties without it still apply: China's **7.5% List 4A** duty, Canada's **50% Section 338** duty on decals and non-lithographic pictures, and Russia's 35% rate. Separately, CBP's **de minimis** exemption for low-value parcels is now suspended for all goods, books included.
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 49 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies and their informational-materials exemption, the Brazil Section 301 tariff, China Section 301 List 4A (List 4B is suspended), the Canada Section 338 duty, Russia's rates in lieu of column 2, the Nicaragua Section 301 phase-in, and the 2025–2026 IEEPA and Section 122 duties that have ended; plus the de minimis changes that decide how low-value printed matter enters. No Section 232 action covers a Chapter 49 line, and the 2019–2021 aircraft-dispute duty on certain UK and German printed matter (9903.89.43) is suspended. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 49 goods fell from **$5.59B in 2024 to $5.16B in 2025** (−7.7%), below the 2022 peak of $5.83B but well above the $4.03B of 2020. **Books (4901) held steady at $2.28B** — 44% of the total — while most other groups shrank: greeting cards and postcards fell 35% to $265M, children's books 13% to $506M, newspapers and periodicals 30% to $102M and unused stamps and banknotes 45% to $45M. Other printed matter (4911: catalogs, posters, pictures, forms) was $1.74B, down 5%.

**China supplied $2.16B (42%)**, down 9%: $833M of books, $644M of other printed matter, **$455M of children's books** — 90% of that line — and $152M of cards. **Canada ($598M) and Mexico ($459M)** ship mostly catalogs and other printed matter (4911) and fell 12% and 10%. The **UK ($430M, 8%)** is the second book supplier. Italy (+12%), India (+5%) and Japan (+33%) grew; Spain fell from $140M to $38M.

Through 2025 most printed matter paid no IEEPA duty because informational materials were excepted, so China's 7.5% List 4A duty was the main extra cost. Since July 24, 2026 the Section 301 tariff on 60 economies applies to goods not entered as informational materials. 2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data.

industryAreas.intro:
Every Chapter 49 line is Free, so the total rate is **the extra duty for the country of origin**. Each cell below is that total for the product group, computed from the current tariff schedule with the same engine as the tariff calculator.

Most cells show two totals. **"Informational materials"** is the rate when the goods are entered as informational materials — books, newspapers, maps, music, posters and similar publications claimed under **9903.05.92** (and 9903.05.09 for Brazil) — which removes the 2026 Section 301 duty and Brazil's 25%. **"Not informational materials"** is the rate without that claim. A claim does not remove **China's 7.5% List 4A duty** on most lines (so Chinese books pay 7.5%, not Free) or **Canada's 50% Section 338 duty** on decals and non-lithographic pictures, which applies even to USMCA goods.

The IEEPA duties (9903.01.xx, 9903.02.xx) are still printed in the schedule but ended February 24, 2026, and the Section 122 surcharge (9903.03.01) expired July 23, 2026; neither is applied. Both excepted informational materials.
China List 4B (9903.88.16) and the 2019–2021 aircraft-dispute duty on certain UK and German printed matter (9903.89.43) are suspended and not applied.
Canada: the 50% Section 338 duty (U.S. note 51) applies whether or not USMCA is claimed; no Chapter 49 line is on the September 29, 2026 import-ban annexes.

Not in the grid: entry rules — the de minimis exemption is suspended for all goods, obscene or treasonous matter is prohibited (19 U.S.C. 1305), piratical copies can be detained — see Import documents.

tariffEngineering.h1: Importing Books & Printed Matter (HTS Ch. 49): Entry Rules, Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Books & Printed Matter into the U.S.: Informational-Materials Exemption, USMCA, De Minimis & Entry Rules (HTS Ch. 49) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: How to import books, newspapers, catalogs and other printed matter: claim 9903.05.92 for informational materials, USMCA for printing done in Canada or Mexico, Chapter 98 provisions for institutions and the blind, plus CBP rules on de minimis, marking, piratical copies and prohibited matter.
keywords: USMCA printed matter rule of origin
books for the blind duty free 9817.00.92

tariffEngineering.intro:
Chapter 49 has no base-rate duty to save, so the levers are about the **extra duties**. The biggest is a claim, not a change of product: books, newspapers, maps, music and other **informational materials** entered under **9903.05.92** pay no 2026 Section 301 duty, and Brazilian ones also claim 9903.05.09. Printing done in **Canada or Mexico** qualifies for USMCA. Some **Chapter 98** provisions (books for the blind, materials for schools and religious institutions, foreign government documents) take goods out of the extra duties entirely.

Entry rules matter as much: CBP's **de minimis** exemption is suspended for all goods, so even a single parcel of books needs an entry; printed matter must be **marked with its country of origin**; CBP can detain **piratical copies** of recorded copyrighted works; and **obscene or treasonous matter** is prohibited (19 U.S.C. 1305).

levers.title: Enter informational materials under 9903.05.92 (and 9903.05.09 for Brazil)
levers.saves: The whole 10%–12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty, and for Brazil the 25% Brazil duty too
levers.appliesTo: Books, newspapers, periodicals, children's books, music, maps, posters, photographs and other publications from any of the 60 economies or Brazil
levers.document: Report 9903.05.92 (and 9903.05.09 for Brazil) on the entry line with the Chapter 49 number, in the order CBP sets: Chapter 98 provision, then the Chapter 99 numbers, then the Chapter 1–97 number. Keep a description of the goods that shows they are publications or similar informational materials.
levers.caveat: It does not lift China's 7.5% List 4A duty, Canada's 50% Section 338 duty, Russia's 35% rate or the Nicaragua duty from 2027. CBP decides whether goods are informational materials; its IEEPA guidance says Chapter 49 goods may qualify, which is not a guarantee for every product (for example blank-form or advertising matter).

levers.title: Claim USMCA on printing done in Canada or Mexico
levers.saves: The 10% Section 301 duty for Canada or Mexico on goods that are not entered as informational materials, such as catalogs, calendars and greeting cards
levers.appliesTo: All 50 lines; the Chapter 49 rule is a change to headings 4901–4911 from any other chapter, so printing on imported paper (Chapter 48) in Canada or Mexico qualifies
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, in any format, with the information listed in 19 CFR 182.12.
levers.caveat: For Canada, USMCA does not remove the 50% Section 338 duty on 4908.90 and 4911.91.40 (U.S. note 51(a)). Reprinting or repackaging finished printed matter is not a change of chapter. The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

finalConclusion.h1: HTS Chapter 49 FAQ: Tariffs on Books, Magazines, Posters & Printed Matter

seo.title: Are Books Exempt from Tariffs? HTS Chapter 49 FAQ 2026: HS Codes for Books, Posters, Greeting Cards, Catalogs | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Answers to what people search about importing printed matter: are books exempt from tariffs, tariffs on books from China, the UK, Canada and Japan, HS codes 4901.99 and 4911.99, posters, greeting cards, catalogs, labels, magazines and de minimis.

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most common questions about importing books, magazines, posters, cards, catalogs and other printed matter into the U.S. — HS codes, tariffs by country and entry rules. Each answer links to the page with the full detail.
keyTakeaways: Every Chapter 49 line — books, newspapers, maps, cards, calendars, catalogs, posters — is Free at the general rate, unchanged since January 2025.
Informational materials entered under 9903.05.92 pay no 2026 Section 301 duty (and 9903.05.09 lifts Brazil's 25%); without the claim, most suppliers pay 10% or 12.5%.
China's 7.5% Section 301 List 4A duty still applies to most Chinese books and printed matter; children's books, religious books, greeting cards and lithographs are on no active China list.
Canada's 50% Section 338 duty hits decals (4908.90) and non-lithographic pictures (4911.91.40) even with USMCA; other USMCA printing enters free.
The IEEPA tariffs never reached informational materials and ended February 24, 2026; de minimis is now suspended for all goods, so low-value book parcels need an entry.

faqs.question: Are books exempt from U.S. tariffs?
searchedAs: are books exempt from tariffs us
are books still exempt from tariffs
faqs.answer: Books have no base duty: every line of heading 4901 is Free. The 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies (10% or 12.5%) do not apply to informational materials entered under 9903.05.92, and Brazil's 25% Section 301 duty has the same exemption (9903.05.09). Two duties have no such exemption: China's 7.5% List 4A duty, which covers most books from China, and Russia's 35% rate. So a UK or Japanese book entered under 9903.05.92 pays $0, and a Chinese one 7.5%.

faqs.question: Were books exempt from Trump's reciprocal and IEEPA tariffs?
searchedAs: are books exempt from trump tariffs
are books exempt from reciprocal tariffs
do trump's tariffs apply to books
faqs.answer: Yes. IEEPA does not allow the President to regulate imports of informational materials (50 U.S.C. 1702(b)(3)), so each 2025 IEEPA order excluded them. Importers used 9903.01.31 for the reciprocal tariff and 9903.01.03, .12 and .22 for Mexico, Canada and China, and CBP said Chapter 49 goods may qualify. Those tariffs ended on February 24, 2026, after the Supreme Court ruled IEEPA does not authorize tariffs.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on books printed in China?
searchedAs: are there tariffs on books from china
tariffs on books printed in china
us tariff on books from china
faqs.answer: Most books from China (4901.99.00) pay 7.5% under Section 301 List 4A (9903.88.15) plus 12.5% under the 2026 Section 301 action (9903.05.31): 20%, or 7.5% when entered as informational materials under 9903.05.92. Bibles and religious books (4901.99.00.40) are excluded from List 4A and pay 12.5% or $0. China shipped $833M of books in 2025.

faqs.question: Are children's books exempt from tariffs?
searchedAs: are children's books exempt from tariffs
faqs.answer: Children's picture, drawing and coloring books (4903.00.00) are Free and are on no active China Section 301 list — List 4B, which named them, is suspended. From China and the other 60 economies they pay 10% or 12.5% under the 2026 Section 301 action unless entered as informational materials under 9903.05.92. China supplied 90% of the $506M imported in 2025.

faqs.question: What are the tariffs on books from the UK, Europe and Japan?
searchedAs: tariffs on books from uk to us
are books from japan exempt from tariffs
faqs.answer: The base rate is Free. The 2026 Section 301 duty is 10% for the UK (9903.05.81), 10% in total for EU countries (9903.05.39) and 12.5% in total for Japan (9903.05.49) — but books, journals and other informational materials entered under 9903.05.92 pay none of it. The 2025 IEEPA rates on these countries ended February 24, 2026.

faqs.question: Are there tariffs on books from Canada?
faqs.answer: Not on books that qualify for USMCA: printing in Canada on paper from another chapter qualifies, and USMCA goods are exempt from Canada's 10% Section 301 duty (9903.05.93). Books are also informational materials (9903.05.92). Canada's 50% Section 338 duty does not cover books; it covers decals (4908.90) and non-lithographic pictures and posters (4911.91.40), even with USMCA.

faqs.question: What is the HTS code for books?
faqs.answer: Heading 4901. Single printed sheets are 4901.10, dictionaries and encyclopedias 4901.91, and other books 4901.99.00, with statistical suffixes for textbooks (.10), bibles and religious books (.40), technical books (.50), art books (.60/.65), hardbound books (.70), rack-size paperbacks (.75) and others by page count (.91–.93). Children's picture books are 4903; brochures devoted to advertising and trade catalogs are 4911. All are Free.

faqs.question: What does HS code 4911 cover (4911.10, 4911.91, 4911.99)?
faqs.answer: Printed matter not covered elsewhere in Chapter 49: 4911.10 trade advertising material, commercial catalogs, price lists and tourist literature; 4911.91 pictures, designs and photographs, including posters, split by age, lithography and thickness; 4911.99 other printed matter — carnets (.20), lithographed items (.60) and other (.80). All Free; 4911 was $1.74B of 2025 imports.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for posters and art prints?
faqs.answer: Printed posters and art prints are 4911.91: lithographed posters printed in the last 20 years are 4911.91.20.20 (up to 0.51 mm thick), other posters 4911.91.40.20, and pictures over 20 years old 4911.91.10. Original engravings, prints and lithographs are 9702. All 4911.91 lines are Free; posters are named in the informational-materials headings, but Canadian 4911.91.40 posters pay the 50% Section 338 duty.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for greeting cards?
searchedAs: us hs code for greeting cards
faqs.answer: 4909.00.40.00 — printed cards bearing personal greetings, messages or announcements, with or without envelopes; printed postcards are 4909.00.20. Both are Free. Greeting cards from China are on no active Section 301 list (List 4B is suspended) and pay 12.5% under the 2026 action; Vietnamese cards also 12.5%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for catalogs and brochures?
faqs.answer: Trade catalogs, price lists and brochures devoted to advertising are 4911.10 (chapter note 5); brochures and leaflets that are not advertising are 4901.10 or 4901.99. Both are Free. Canada and Mexico shipped mostly 4911 goods in 2025, and USMCA-qualifying catalogs enter free.

faqs.question: Are there tariffs on magazines and newspapers?
faqs.answer: Magazines, journals and newspapers are heading 4902, Free. They are informational materials, so 9903.05.92 removes the 2026 Section 301 duty; from China they still pay 7.5% under List 4A. Bound volumes and multi-issue sets are classified as books (4901). Imports fell 30% to $102M in 2025.

faqs.question: Are printed labels and stickers in Chapter 49?
searchedAs: hs code for printed paper labels
faqs.answer: Paper labels, printed or not, are heading 4821 in Chapter 48: printed labels are 4821.10 (lithographed .20, other .40) and unprinted self-adhesive labels 4821.90.20, all Free. Chapter 49 covers decals that transfer a design (4908), and other printed matter (4911). Classify by what the article is, and get a CBP ruling if unsure.

faqs.question: Can books still be shipped duty-free under de minimis?
faqs.answer: No longer by default. From August 29, 2025 the executive orders suspending de minimis kept it for informational materials, but CBP's June 24, 2026 rules suspend the $800 exemption for all merchandise, by mail (19 CFR 145.31) and every other mode (19 CFR 10.151), and a 2025 law ends it on July 1, 2027. Books still owe no base duty, but each shipment needs an entry.

faqs.question: How much printed matter does the U.S. import, and from where?
faqs.answer: $5.16B in 2025, down 7.7% from $5.59B. Books were $2.28B (44%), other printed matter $1.74B and children's books $506M. China supplied 42%, Canada 12%, Mexico 9%, the UK 8%, Italy 4% and India 3%.
